authored_description: Table 17-9 is the primary first-order sizing tool for a passive optical sensor system. Starting from a target ground sampling distance (GSD) and orbital altitude, it chains through six calculation sections to produce a complete sensor parameter set: orbit geometry and swath width (Section A), pixel parameters and data rate (Section B), detector integration time (Section C), optics sizing including focal length, aperture diameter, f-number, and MTF (Section D), full radiometric chain from scene radiance through SNR and dynamic range (Section E), and noise equivalent temperature difference for thermal IR systems (Section F, incomplete in this version). Key user inputs are orbital altitude, target GSD, detector pixel size, operating wavelength, quality factor Q, and scene temperature. Key outputs are aperture diameter, focal length, data rate, integration time, and SNR. Use this table at the concept design phase to establish whether a mission resolution and sensitivity requirements are physically achievable before committing to a detailed optical design. Note that atmospheric transmissivity input is required for Section E — use MODTRAN or published transmissivity curves for your wavelength band. Section F (NEDT) is a stub in this version and requires supplementary calculation for thermal IR missions.
